subbench.objective: What an engine pays to EDIT a large text file: the cost of a global substitution over a few-hundred-MB Apache access log, split by what dominates it -- copying (a literal), searching (a rare two-literal alternation), per-match output (every digit run), capture rearrangement, class-heavy masking (IPv4, e-mail), a case-forcing template, and a backreference inside a negative lookahead with a conditional template (the VM-only, DFA-refusing shape). The answer is an OUTPUT BYTE STRING, so the correctness gate is its sha256 against the libpcre2 oracle's.

testee.build_flags: RE2 has no runtime version API (confirmed absent, re2.h read in full); engine_version is pkg-config's re2.pc Version field (the library's soname/ABI version). The Debian package 20250805-1build3 (RE2's own upstream snapshot date, its de facto release identifier) rides here for full provenance.
testee.compile_cost_definition: eager-jit-adjacent (capability_set_v1.md 7.1/7.2): the explicit RE2(pattern, options) CONSTRUCTOR call, timed in-driver (`compile`). CAVEAT: unlike pcre2-jit's pcre2_jit_compile, this call does NOT build the runtime DFA -- RE2's DFA is built LAZILY at first match, cached, and can be flushed and rebuilt under max_mem pressure (re2.h). A reader pooling this testee beside pcre2-jit under one eager-jit table is comparing two different compile-cost SHAPES that happen to share a class token; the reporter's 7.2 footnote fires on exactly this definition-string mismatch. Median of N with spread is the REPORTER's reduction.

ncapturegroups.description: lexical capturing groups in the pattern (the overall match, group 0, is not counted -- re2.h's own convention)

program_size.description: the forward Prog's size -- requirements 4.2's 'program size' for this engine. re2.h's own words: 'a very approximate measure of a regexp's cost'. NOT the runtime DFA, which is built lazily at match time (capability_set_v1.md 7.1)

refusal_class.description: 'size-limit' for ErrorPatternTooLarge; 'syntax' for every other named ErrorCode; ABSENT when the diagnostic carries no parseable code
refusal_class.source: the RE2::ErrorCode name the driver embeds in its `error` line on a did-not-compile outcome, bucketed by this adapter's REFUSAL_CLASS table (capability_set_v1.md 5.5: 'declared ONLY by a config whose engine gives a closed, structural signal' -- RE2::ErrorCode is exactly that)

reverse_program_size.description: the reverse Prog's size, used as the second phase of an unanchored search (re2.h); RE2 has two programs where pcre2/pcrec have one, so this is declared as its own pair rather than folded into program_size
